items.title: 1兆行を100円未満でクエリする ― 2年前の「1兆行チャレンジ」をClickHouse Cloudで再検証
items.summary: 「1兆行チャレンジ」は、S3上に置かれた2.4TiB・10万ファイルのParquet、合計1兆行をいかに高速に集計できるかという挑戦です。当時、AWSのスポットインスタンスでClickHouseクラスタを組み、1兆行を集計するクエリが3分未満、コストは100円未満でこれを達成しました。本セッションでは、同じ挑戦をClickHouse Cloudでやり直します。カラムナストレージと圧縮、分散並列処理、ベクトル化実行といった技術が、なぜこれほど高速で低コストな処理を実現できるのかを解説しつつ、この2年で入ったParquetリーダーの刷新や並列レプリカも踏まえて、この記録を計り直し、その結果を解説します。

items.title: Computational checks (Return tests, types, and lint through Hooks) | Learn Harness Engineering with Kiro 04
items.summary: Level 300. Tests, types, lint, and structural tests give the same result for the same input, so this deck runs them in a Kiro hook as Kiro finishes its answer and returns how to fix what fails. On a small booking app, it shows a check that counts the booking's row in the DB, test output in a few lines that Kiro can act on, and a hook that blocks deleting a test file. This is deck 04 (Check pillar) of the "Learn Harness Engineering with Kiro" series.

items.title: Hooks and lifecycle controls (Events, limits, and cancellation) | Learn Strands Agents with Kiro 03
items.summary: A deck for Python developers who have built a first agent with Strands Agents and now want to control each call. It caps one call with limits, stops it from outside with cancel_signal, reads stop_reason, and shows what happens to tool errors, hook errors, and overlapping calls. It then registers hooks with add_hook, HookProvider, and Plugin, changes event properties to redact input, swap or cap tools, retry a tool, and resume, and compares middleware (Input, Wrap, Output) with retry strategies, with diagrams, real code, and real output. The facts come from the official Strands Agents documentation only, and the examples use a help-desk agent with made-up customers and orders, made for this series and run on Amazon Bedrock in the Tokyo Region. As of November 2026 (Strands Agents 1.64, Level 300). This is deck 03 (Go deeper) of the Learn Strands Agents with Kiro series.

items.title: Tools and MCP (@tool, vended tools, and MCP servers) | Learn Strands Agents with Kiro 02
items.summary: This Level 200 deck shows a Python developer who is new to Strands Agents how to give an agent tools: @tool functions, the vended tools that ship with the SDK, direct calls through agent.tool, concurrent and sequential tool executors, and class-based and async tools, with architecture diagrams, flow figures and the real output of each sample run on Amazon Bedrock in the Tokyo Region. It then connects the agent to MCP servers with MCPClient (stdio and Streamable HTTP, a client for a server protected by AWS IAM SigV4, several servers with prefix and tool_filters) and shows how a docstring and type hints become the tool spec, how return values become tool results and how invocation_state passes values outside the prompt, as deck 02 (Get started) of the series Learn Strands Agents with Kiro.

items.title: Find and share across teams (AWS Agent Registry) | Learn Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Kiro 12
items.summary: This Level 300 deck shows how AWS Agent Registry lets teams publish the agents, tools and skills they build so that others in the company find only approved ones, with the help desk agent of a made-up online electronics shop: an English registry in the Tokyo Region with IAM inbound auth and manual approval, the AgentCore Gateway of deck 04 put in as an MCP record and approved by a curator, a search with the AWS CLI and with the MCP endpoint of the registry that finds it by words not in the record, and unsigned requests that are refused, all with real terminal screens and figures that use the official AWS icons. It then covers the four roles and their IAM permissions, the record life cycle, approval notices through Amazon EventBridge, organization auto-detection, sharing with AWS RAM and AWS PrivateLink, clean-up and pricing, as deck 12 (Govern and share) of the series Learn Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Kiro.
